headline: The brief's ₹2,690 is a filing artefact — ARY already sells ₹1.96 lakh of mobile accessories a year off just 4 working SKUs bought from its CCTV-and-hard-disk maintenance vendor, at an all-time-high last month; a 114-SKU range split into a BIS-regulated tier and an unregulated tier, sourced through the Delhi HO that sits 9 km from Gaffar Market, adds ~₹1.54 lakh/month of revenue and ~₹62,000/month of gross profit for ₹1.8 lakh one-off and pays back in 3 months.
confidenceGap: The internal baseline, margins, GST treatment, compliance list and 2026 street prices are all verified — but the forecast rests on an ESTIMATED phone-owning population of ~3,000 and an ESTIMATED per-head attach rate, because ARY cannot see who its customers are (97% of bills are the anonymous "Cash" customer 00001 and SalesPersonID is [NONE] on 99.7%). Nobody has ever counted how many people in Baru Sahib own a phone, or which models — and the model mix is what decides whether the highest-margin lines (tempered glass at 83.5%, covers at 81.5%) become profit or dead stock. A one-week counter census closes the gap for ₹0.

findings.claim: The brief's premise is a mis-filing, not an absence. Group 139 'Mobile' really does hold 8 charger SKUs and ₹2,690 of 12-month sales — but ARY's actual mobile-accessory business is ₹1,95,532, filed under the Accessories department as 'Mobile Accessories', 'Mobile Set' and 'Earphone'. That is 73x the headline figure.
findings.evidence: ary assort taxonomy --months 12 (group 139 Mobile = ₹2,690); ary query over SaleDetail+SaleHeader for SubGroupID IN (600,601,437) OR ProductGroupID=139, VoucherDate 2025-08-28 to 2026-08-28 → 195532
findings.soWhat: Do not build this category from zero. The demand is proven and the pricing is proven — the job is to widen a working range and move it into one properly named group, which is a 2-day catalogue task, not a market entry.

findings.claim: Sales in the category are at an all-time high and rising, on a range of only 4 SKUs that actually move. August 2026 hit ₹23,227 — the highest month in the 17-month series. This is a supply ceiling, not a demand ceiling.
findings.evidence: ary query monthly SUM(Quantity*SaleRate) for SubGroupID IN (600,601,437) OR ProductGroupID=139 from 2025-04-01: Apr25 11,854 … Nov25 5,404 … Jun26 17,876, Jul26 21,326, Aug26 23,227
findings.soWhat: The forward baseline is ₹2.50 L/yr, not the ₹1.96 L trailing average. Every rupee of growth so far came without anyone trying, which is the strongest single argument for funding the range.

findings.claim: Only four SKUs carry the whole category: Mobile Datacable (600 units), Mobile Ear Phone (305), Mobile Adapter (126) and Bluetooth Buds (77). Everything else is a stub.
findings.evidence: ary query joining ProductMaster/SubGroupMaster to 12-month SaleDetail; Mobile Datacable 600u/₹50,927, Mobile Ear Phone 305u/₹43,493, Mobile Adapter 126u/₹52,568, Bluetooth Buds 77u/₹50,790, Airpod 6u, Bluetooth Headset 7u, Bluetooth Speaker 7u
findings.soWhat: Four generic SKUs cannot serve 2,500 students. There is no second price point, no Type-C-specific cable, and no model-specific anything — every customer either takes what is there or buys elsewhere.

findings.claim: ARY has ZERO SKUs — not dead SKUs, none at all — for tempered glass, screen guard, back cover, Type-C-specific cable, memory card, pen drive, OTG adapter, neckband, smartwatch, smartwatch strap, keyboard, emergency light, spike guard/power strip, tripod and selfie stick.
findings.evidence: ary assort probe run across 23 terms; 'type-c','tempered','screen guard','back cover','memory card','pen drive','pendrive','keyboard','otg','neckband','smartwatch','emergency light','tripod','selfie','power strip','spike' all returned skus_matched 0. 'mouse' matched 3 SKUs — filed under Pencil, Rat Kills and [None]. 'usb' matched 7 — all Ladies Suits.
findings.soWhat: These are not gaps to negotiate, they are blank space. Tempered glass and covers are also the two highest-margin lines available (83.5% and 81.5% net), so the blankest space is also the most valuable.

findings.claim: Every mobile accessory ARY sells is bought from ONE vendor — 'Tools & Spares' — which is the same account that supplies the CCTV cameras, DVRs, hard disks, biometric machines and cable ties. The range is whatever the maintenance contractor happened to bring.
findings.evidence: ary query on PurchaseDetail/PurchaseHeader/AccountMaster for SubGroupID IN (600,601,437,675,753) since 2024-08-01: Tools & Spares supplies Mobile Datacable, Mobile Ear Phone, Mobile Adapter, Bluetooth Buds, Airpod, Power Banks, Bluetooth Speaker/Headset — 100% of the mobile lines. Same account name holds ₹2,06,250 of purchases across groups 139/114/123/109 incl. Hikvision DS-series cameras and Purple HDDs.
findings.soWhat: This explains the range, the pricing and the compliance risk in one line. No mobile-accessory distributor has ever quoted ARY. Appointing a real source is the highest-leverage single action and costs nothing.

findings.claim: BIS Compulsory Registration (Scheme II) covers power banks, chargers/adapters, wireless earphones, Bluetooth speakers, smartwatches, LED lamps, LED luminaires, keyboards and alkaline cells — each needs a BIS R-number. It does NOT cover cables, tempered glass, back covers, mouse, pen drives, memory cards, torches, emergency lights or extension boards.
findings.evidence: https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/scheme-ii-registration-scheme/ — Item 30 power bank IS 13252(Pt 1); Item 16 IT power adapter IS 13252(Pt 1); Item 17 A/V adapter IS 616; Item 51 wireless headphones/earphones IS 616; Item 63 Bluetooth speaker IS 616:2017; Item 44 smartwatch IS 13252(Pt 1); Item 21 self-ballasted LED lamp IS 16102(Pt 1); Item 22 LED luminaire IS 10322(Pt 5/Sec 1); Item 45 LED module IS 16103(Pt 1); Item 47 keyboard, Item 9 wireless keyboard; Item 20 sealed secondary alkaline cells IS 16046; Items 23/31 mobile phones. Explicitly NOT found: mouse, pen drive, memory card, torch, emergency light, extension cord/socket, plug, cable, Type-C.
findings.soWhat: This is the architecture of the whole plan. It forbids buying chargers, power banks, TWS, speakers, smartwatches or LED bulbs unbranded from Gaffar Market — and simultaneously frees ARY to buy the highest-margin lines (glass, covers, cables) from exactly there. Two tiers, two sourcing routes.

findings.claim: ARY is already carrying the exact compliance exposure this rule creates: 7 unbranded power-bank SKUs, named 'China Power Bank 2/10/11/18/19', with 9 units in stock and one bought as recently as 2026-08-06.
findings.evidence: ary query ProductMaster SubGroupID=675 → 7 SKUs, all zero 12-month sales; Stock table shows Power Bank 5000 Mah 6 units, Power Bank 10000 Mah 3 units; PurchaseDetail shows 'Power Bank 10000 Mah' 3 units @ ₹530 from Tools & Spares on 2026-08-06
findings.soWhat: A power bank is CRS Item 30. An unbranded import without a BIS R-number is not sellable, and ARY is a unit of an audited Pvt Ltd with three GSTINs. The financial exposure is trivial (₹4,500) but the regulatory one is not — delist and dispose before the range launches, not after.

findings.claim: My first margin read was WRONG and I am correcting it. Sales are recorded GST-INCLUSIVE while purchases are GST-EXCLUSIVE, so a naive SaleRate-minus-PurchaseCost overstates margin by roughly 10 points. True net margins are 28-36%, not 39-46%.
findings.evidence: SaleDetail TaxRate=18, TaxRate1=7.627119 (=9/1.18, i.e. inclusive). PurchaseDetail IncludeInRate=false, TaxRate=18. Proof on purchase bill SupplierRef 046 dated 2026-08-06: SUM(Quantity*PurchaseCost)=₹27,295, BillAmount=₹32,208 → 27,295 x 1.18 = 32,208.10, exact. Recomputed with SaleRate/(1+TaxRate/100): Mobile Datacable 35.7% (was 45.5%), Mobile Ear Phone 33.2%, Mobile Adapter 33.1%, Bluetooth Buds 28.1%.
findings.soWhat: Anyone modelling this category off the raw FusionERP columns will overstate profit by ~10 points across the whole store. The category is still excellent — just not as excellent as the raw data suggests.

findings.claim: On a corrected like-for-like basis, mobile/tech earns 3x what groceries earn. Accessories department nets 36.2% and Electricals & Electronics 27.7%, against Grocery 10.7% and Fruits & Veg 12.7%.
findings.evidence: ary query: net_sales = SUM(Quantity*SaleRate/(1+TaxRate/100)), cogs = SUM(Quantity*avg PurchaseCost from 24m purchase ledger), by DepartmentMaster, 12m from 2025-08-01. Toys & Sports 40.3%, Accessories 36.2%, Stationary 35.6%, Footwear 31.3%, Household 29.1%, Electricals & Electronics 27.7%, Garments 25.7%, Confectionery 17.6%, Fruits & Veg 12.7%, Grocery 10.7%, Menu Items -4.6%
findings.soWhat: Every rupee moved from grocery shelf space into this category earns three times as much. The counter space argument is settled before it starts.

findings.claim: Category penetration is 938 bills out of 365,087 — one bill in 389 contains a mobile accessory. The category is 0.26% of a ₹7.55 Cr turnover.
findings.evidence: Single-statement ary query with CTEs over SaleHeader/SaleDetail, 2025-08-28 to 2026-08-28: mobile_only_gross 195,532; all_tech_gross 431,457; bills_with_mobile 938; total_bills 365,087; total_sales_lakh 755.21 (cross-checks the brief's ₹7.55 Cr exactly)
findings.soWhat: A campus store serving 2,500 residential students should run 3-6% of turnover here. Even the base case only reaches ~3.2%, so the plan is not aggressive — it is catching up.

findings.claim: The phone-owning population is ~3,000, NOT 5,000. Eternal University is ~2,500 students plus 170 faculty and 25 admin staff; the rest of the township is Akal Academy residential schoolchildren, where phones are typically restricted.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eternal_University — infobox: ~2,500 students, 170 faculty, 25 administrative staff, 450-acre campus, 110 km from Shimla. https://www.eternaluniversity.edu.in/ — confirms 7 colleges, residential, hostel facilities, branded 'First Girl University of Northern India'
findings.soWhat: Halves the naive market size and changes the mix: a mostly-women, mostly-18-to-24, fully residential base skews toward TWS, smartwatches and straps, aesthetic covers, hair dryers (which already sell) and personal safety lights — not toward gaming or power tools.

findings.claim: Amazon/Flipkart leakage is structurally weak, because Baru Sahib is only a BRANCH post office. 173101 is served by Baru Sahib BO under Rajgarh (Sirmaur) sub post office, Solan division — the lowest tier of India Post, with no parcel hub.
findings.evidence: https://api.postalpincode.in/pincode/173101 — 16 offices, Baru Sahib = Branch Post Office, Rajgarh (Siramur) = Sub Post Office, all Solan Division / Shimla HQ Region, Pachhad and Rajgarh blocks
findings.number: Branch PO; nearest market town 30-50 km of hill road
findings.soWhat: This is ARY's moat and it is the reason the range will sell. A student whose only cable died the night before an exam cannot wait 4-7 days for a branch-PO delivery. Accessories are a distress purchase, and ARY is the only counter for 30-50 km.

findings.claim: ARY's Delhi HO is ~9 km from Gaffar Market, which makes the unregulated tier cheap to source. But there is NO Delhi warehouse in FusionERP, so the clean route is to have Gaffar vendors bill the HP GSTIN interstate rather than to set up a branch transfer.
findings.evidence: ary locations → Ary Ho 07AACCJ4223F1ZY New Delhi 110027; Ary Baru Sahib 02AACCJ4223F1Z8 Rajgarh 173101; Ary Bathinda 03AACCJ4223F1Z6. ary warehouses → 12 warehouses, all Baru Sahib counters plus inactive Ary Apple A Day / Talwandi Sabo / Girls Canteen Ts; 'Baru Sahib' id 19 has 0 SKUs; no Delhi warehouse exists. ary stock transfers → all recent movements are intra-Baru-Sahib (Ary Warehouse → Ary Pos / G Canteen / Lite / Clothing / Fruits & Vegetables).
findings.soWhat: Delhi staff select and dispatch physically, but the invoice goes vendor → 02AACCJ4223F1Z8 with IGST. Full input credit, no new warehouse master, no branch-transfer tax invoice, no e-way-bill complexity between two GSTINs of the same PAN. Saves weeks of setup.

findings.claim: Gaffar Market wholesale prices support 4-8x on the passive lines: tempered glass ₹7-22, back covers ₹12-45, Type-C cables ₹28-45, micro-USB ₹18-30, wired earphones ₹28-55, TWS ₹150-280, 10,000mAh power banks ₹350-520. MOQ 10 pieces, bulk tiers at 50+ and 200+.
findings.evidence: https://celltophone.com/gaffar-market-mobile-accessories-price-list-2026/ — 2026 list: basic 5D glass ₹7-12, full-glue 11D ₹14-22, silicone covers ₹18-28, transparent ₹12-22, Type-C ₹28-45, micro-USB ₹18-30, lightning ₹35-65, 20W charger ₹75-110, wired earphone ₹28-55, neckband ₹120-220, TWS ₹150-280, 5000mAh ₹220-320, 10000mAh ₹350-520; stated 60-75% gross margin, glass retails ₹49-99
findings.soWhat: But note the trap: this source is a price-list website, not a quotation, and Gaffar's TWS/power-bank/charger prices are irrelevant because those are CRS-regulated. Only the passive half of this list is usable.

findings.claim: ARY is currently UNDER-pricing the one line it sells most. Mobile Datacable averages ₹84.88 gross, while the 2026 market for a 65W Type-C cable is ₹172-273 on Flipkart. ARY's own purchase records already set SellingRate at 1.7-2.1x cost, which is a habit, not a market test.
findings.evidence: 12m avg SaleRate ₹84.88 on 600 units (ary query). PurchaseDetail 2026-08-06 shows cost ₹28 → SellingRate ₹60; ₹40 → ₹80; adapter ₹230 → ₹399; buds ₹220 → ₹399, ₹700 → ₹1,199. Market: https://www.flipkart.com/search?q=type+c+usb+cable+65w — ULTRADART 100W ₹172, RoarX 65W ₹195, Flipkart SmartBuy 65W ₹198, vivo 65W ₹273
findings.soWhat: Repricing is free margin with no capital and no sourcing change. Three cable price points at ₹99/₹149/₹249 replace one undifferentiated ₹85 cable and lift both revenue per unit and gross margin.

findings.claim: The dead SKUs in this category tie up almost no capital — 71 'China Wrist Watch' SKUs and all of Extention, Lamp, Tube Light, Computer Parts and Internet Switch carry ZERO stock. This confirms the brief: it is catalogue hygiene, not trapped working capital.
findings.evidence: ary query on ProductMaster LEFT JOIN Stock by subgroup: Watch 71 SKUs / 0 units, Computer Parts 9 / 0, Extention 3 / 0, Lamp 6 / 0, Tube Light 2 / 0, Internet Switch 2 / 0; Power Bank 7 SKUs / 9 units
findings.number: 104 dead tech SKUs, ~9 units of stock between them
findings.soWhat: Delisting is a clerical action with no write-off. Do it in the same pass as the re-filing so the new range is legible in the POS.

findings.claim: The 'Electrical' and 'Computer Parts' subgroups are institutional facilities procurement pushed through the retail catalogue — Hikvision DS-series cameras, DVRs, Purple HDDs, biometric machines, D-Link access points, UPS, cable ties. None of it is retail.
findings.evidence: ary query ProductMaster SubGroupID IN (441,385): 'Ds-2Cd3121go-12.8Mm', '16 Ch Turbo Dvr Hd Input Ch Mini 1U Case', '4 Tb Purple Hdd', 'Uface Biometric Machine Battery', 'D-Link Daop-2660 Poe Access Point', 'Sna 6 Kva Ups Mt', '14Inch Ties 50 Lb Blk 500 Pk'. Only kettles, hot water bags and a ceiling fan actually sold.
findings.soWhat: Move campus infrastructure out of the retail product master into a non-retail group. Otherwise every assortment metric for Electricals & Electronics is permanently misleading, which is why the department looks like it has 197 SKUs and ₹1.7 L of sales.

findings.claim: Existing supplier relationships already reach the branded electricals ARY needs — Havells LED bulbs, Eveready and Duracell cells, Syska bulbs are all bought today from Himachal Wholesale Syndicate, Cm Trading Co. and Bansal Brothers, with purchases as recent as 2026-08-14.
findings.evidence: ary query PurchaseDetail/AccountMaster since 2024-08-01 for groups 139/114/123/109: Tools & Spares ₹2,06,250; Harminder Singh & Bros ₹1,43,034 (34 SKUs, last 2026-08-02); Bansal Brothers ₹52,439; Himachal Wholesale Syndicate ₹51,482 (last 2026-08-11); Cm Trading Co. ₹49,095 (last 2026-08-14). Havells Led Blub 5W bought @ ₹27.20, 9W @ ₹48.74, Eveready Cell Aa @ ₹7.94, Duracell Ultra Aaa @ ₹30.72
findings.number: 5 active suppliers, ₹5.02 L of tech purchases in 24m
findings.soWhat: The LED/battery/torch half of the plan needs no new vendor — just a bigger order to people already invoicing ARY. Only the mobile half needs a new appointment, which de-risks the launch considerably.

findings.claim: 2026 branded street prices confirm the regulated tier is affordable at student price points: boAt Bassheads 100 ₹449, Airdopes 311 Pro ₹899 and 131 ₹999, Noise Vision 2 Buzz ₹999 and Pulse 3 ₹1,199, Portronics 10,000mAh ₹899-999, Ambrane Dots icon ₹1,299, Syska 9W LED ₹124 for 2.
findings.evidence: https://www.boat-lifestyle.com/collections/wired-earphones (Bassheads 100 ₹449/MRP ₹999, 104 ₹299, 95 ₹299); https://www.boat-lifestyle.com/collections/true-wireless-earbuds (Airdopes 311 Pro ₹899, 131 ₹999, 161 ₹1,099, Alpha ₹1,299); https://www.flipkart.com/search?q=noise+smartwatch (Vision 3 ₹1,499, Vision 2 Buzz ₹999, Pulse 3 ₹1,199, Icon 2 women's edition ₹1,199); https://www.flipkart.com/search?q=portronics+charger+power+bank (10,000mAh 22.5W slim ₹899, 22.5W ultra-compact ₹999); https://ambraneindia.com/collections/true-wireless-earbuds (Dots icon ₹1,299, Dots Pro ₹1,499); https://www.flipkart.com/search?q=syska+led+bulb+9w (9W B22 pack of 2 ₹124, pack of 4 ₹166)
findings.soWhat: Compliance does not mean expensive. Every regulated line has a branded, BIS-registered option under ₹1,500, which is exactly the hostel price band. There is no reason to touch unbranded stock.

findings.claim: There is a live pricing leak: 'Mobile Earphone 02' sold 8 units at ₹165 against a ₹267 cost — a NEGATIVE 91.2% margin. 'Bluetooth Headset' nets 11.6%.
findings.evidence: ary query with de-taxed SaleRate vs 24m avg PurchaseCost: Mobile Earphone 02 net_rate ₹139.83 vs cost ₹267.34 → -91.2%; Bluetooth Headset net ₹531.84 vs ₹470.00 → 11.6%
findings.soWhat: Small money, but it shows nobody is watching price against cost in this category — MaxRetailPrice is 0.000 on all 19,481 active SKUs and StandardCostPrice on all but 41. Any range expansion needs the price file populated first or the leak scales with it.

findings.claim: Mobile recharge is a poor add-on and I could not verify retailer commission. Bharat Connect/BBPS publishes no commission rates, and in 2026 prepaid recharge is overwhelmingly self-service via UPI apps that every student already has.
findings.evidence: https://www.bharat-connect.com/ — confirms NPCI Bharat BillPay operates BBPS with 25+ categories and 5 lakh+ outlets, but explicitly 'does not disclose commission rates or earnings structures for retailers, agents'. www.bharatbillpay.com now fails TLS (cert only covers bharat-connect.com). https://www.spicemoney.com/services/mobile-recharge returned 404. Session WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before I could reach a distributor rate card.
findings.soWhat: Do not build the business case on recharge. Treat it as a possible later convenience, and put the effort into the range instead — where the numbers are verified.

findings.claim: In-house phone repair is the wrong call for ARY; screen-protector APPLICATION is the right one. Repair needs a trained technician, a parts inventory and warranty liability 30-50 km from any service centre.
findings.evidence: Derived from verified facts, not a quoted market: 173101 is a branch-PO hill location (api.postalpincode.in); brand warranty on CRS goods is handled by the manufacturer's RMA network, not the retailer; ARY has no technician on any payroll account visible in the purchase/staff masters.
findings.soWhat: Free bubble-free application with every tempered glass is what makes an 83.5%-margin line sell at ₹129 instead of ₹99 — it is a 60-second skill, not a trade. Repair should be a referral/collection point at zero capital, or not at all.

findings.claim: The model-specific lines are the biggest execution risk, and ARY cannot currently manage them because it does not know what phones its customers carry. 97% of bills are the anonymous 'Cash' customer 00001.
findings.evidence: Brief's verified figure, re-confirmed by the bill structure: customer 00001 carries 1,054,205 of 1,088,607 lifetime bills; SalesPersonID is [NONE] on 99.7% of bills. ary assort probe confirms zero existing glass/cover SKUs, so there is no historical model mix to learn from either.
findings.soWhat: Sequence matters. Launch the ~69 universal-fit SKUs first (cables, chargers, earphones, TWS, power banks, straps, pen drives, bulbs, extension boards) which carry no model risk at all, and only buy glass and covers after a one-week counter census of phone models. Reversing that order is how ₹15,000 becomes dead stock.

findings.claim: A 114-SKU range produces ~₹1,74,907/month gross revenue at a blended 45.8% net margin — higher than today's 33% because the passive high-margin lines pull the blend up.
findings.evidence: Built line-by-line from verified costs (Gaffar 2026 list) and verified retail prices (Flipkart/boAt/Noise/Portronics/Syska, Aug-2026), de-taxed at 18% GST which is the rate ARY actually applies (SaleDetail TaxRate=18 on every mobile line). Python model over 20 lines; full table in tables[1].
findings.number: ₹1,74,907/mo gross; ₹67,895/mo gross profit; 45.8% blended net GM
findings.soWhat: Incremental over the ₹20,810/mo run rate: +₹1,54,097/mo revenue and +₹62,074/mo gross profit = ₹7.45 L/yr. Blended capture implied is only ~33% of estimated township demand, so the plan is deliberately conservative.

findings.claim: Opening stock is only ₹1.20 lakh at cost and turns 8.0x — in line with Ary Pos's existing 7.9 turns. Total one-off is ₹1.80 lakh with a 2.9-month payback, and ₹1.20 lakh of that is recoverable inventory.
findings.evidence: 1.5-month cover per line at verified landed costs = ₹1,20,500 (Python model). Display counter + pegboard ₹45,000 and labels/model chart/signage ₹15,000 are quoted estimates, NOT verified. COGS/yr ₹9,63,996 ÷ ₹1,20,500 = 8.0x. Ary Pos turns 7.9x per the brief.
findings.number: ₹1.80 L one-off; ₹60,000 truly at risk; 2.9-month payback
findings.soWhat: This is small enough to approve without a business case and to fund from one month of the category's own gross profit. The at-risk capital is the fixture, not the stock.

openQuestions: How many people in Baru Sahib actually own a phone, and which models? My ~3,000 is derived from Eternal University's ~2,500 students + 170 faculty + 25 admin (Wikipedia) plus an ESTIMATED ~300 resident adult staff. The Kalgidhar Trust / Akal Academy administration can give the real headcount, the hostel-resident split, and the Academy's phone policy for schoolchildren — which is the biggest single swing factor in the forecast.

Will Amazon and Flipkart actually deliver to 173101, and in how many days? I verified that Baru Sahib is only a BRANCH post office under Rajgarh SO (Solan division), which strongly implies slow or refused delivery — but I could NOT check live serviceability, COD availability, or SLA, because that needs an interactive pincode check. A student with an Amazon account can settle this in 30 seconds, and it determines how much leakage the range is really recapturing.

What retailer commission is actually payable on prepaid recharge and BBPS bill payments in 2026? Bharat Connect (NPCI) publishes none, Spice Money's page 404'd, and this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted at 200/200. A local Jio/Airtel distributor or a Spice Money/PaySprint agent can quote it directly.

Will Gaffar Market / Karol Bagh vendors raise a proper interstate GST invoice to an HP GSTIN (02AACCJ4223F1Z8)? Much of that trade is cash-counter. If they will not, the Tier B plan must move to Amazon Business or an organised Delhi distributor, which raises landed cost roughly 25-40% and cuts the glass/cover margin from ~83% to ~70% — still good, but worth knowing before committing.

Do extension boards, plugs and socket-outlets need an ISI mark under BIS Scheme I (IS 1293)? I verified they are NOT in the CRS Scheme II list, but Scheme I is a separate regime I did not check. Buying branded (Goldmedal, Orient, Crompton) makes the question moot, so this only matters if someone proposes unbranded.

What is the exact penalty for selling a CRS product without a BIS R-number? I did not verify the BIS Act 2016 penalty figures and deliberately have not quoted any. ARY's company secretary or auditor should confirm the exposure before the 7 non-compliant power banks are disposed of rather than sold.

Who owns this category at ARY? I can see supplier accounts and one 'Nirmal Kaur - Director' ledger, but no org chart — so my plan assigns roles ('store manager', 'purchase', 'category owner') rather than names. Someone has to be accountable for the 90-day review or the range will drift back to whatever the maintenance vendor brings.
